name: When is it time to replace a bathtub instead of refinishing it?

mainEntity.name: When is it time to replace a bathtub instead of refinishing it?

acceptedAnswer.text: Replacing an existing tub is recommended when you notice persistent leaks around the perimeter, deep structural cracks in the basin, or soft spots in the subfloor beneath the unit. Outdated tubs with worn, porous enamel that harbor recurring mildew or resist cleaning are also primary candidates for replacement. If your family needs better accessibility or wishes to convert a tub into a walk-in shower or modern soaking basin, replacement is often more cost-effective than ongoing surface repairs.
acceptedAnswer.description: Replace your tub if there are structural cracks, chronic leaks, damaged subflooring, or deeply worn surfaces where short-term refinishing will not hold up.
